questions.text:
यहाँ दो कथन दिए गए हैं अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) :
अभिकथन (A): साझेदारों के स्थायी पूँजी खाते सदैव जमा शेष दर्शाते हैं, जो वर्ष-दर-वर्ष एकसमान (स्थायी) रहते हैं जब तक कि उसमें कोई पूँजी न जोड़ी जाए अथवा पूँजी का आहरण न किया जाए।
कारण (R) : जब पूँजी स्थायी होती है, तो विभिन्न मदों, जैसे लाभ अथवा हानि का भाग, पूँजी पर ब्याज, आहरण, आहरण पर ब्याज इत्यादि का लेखा साझेदारों के पूँजी खातों में किया जाता है।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
There are two statements Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): The partners' fixed capital accounts always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital.
Reason (R): When captials are fixed, then various items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded in partners' capital accounts.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, लेकिन कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, लेकिन कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, लेकिन कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is incorrect, but Reason (R) is correct.

questions.solution: The Assertion (A) is correct because under the fixed capital method, the capital account balance remains unchanged unless there is an introduction of additional capital or withdrawal of capital. The Reason (R) is incorrect because when capitals are fixed, items like share of profit, interest on capital, and drawings are recorded in the Partners' Current Accounts, not the Capital Accounts. Thus, option (C) is the correct answer.
questions.solution_hindi: अभिकथन (A) सही है क्योंकि स्थायी पूँजी पद्धति के अंतर्गत पूँजी खाते का शेष तब तक अपरिवर्तित रहता है जब तक कि अतिरिक्त पूँजी न लगाई जाए या पूँजी का आहरण न किया जाए। कारण (R) ग़लत है क्योंकि जब पूँजी स्थायी होती है, तो लाभ का भाग, पूँजी पर ब्याज और आहरण जैसी मदों का लेखा साझेदारों के चालू खातों (Current Accounts) में किया जाता है, न कि पूँजी खातों में। इसलिए, सही विकल्प (C) है।

sub_questions.text_english: Ravita, Savita, Kavita and Babita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 3:2:2. On $1^{st}$ April, 2024 Savita retired and her share was acquired equally by the remaining partners. The new profit sharing ratio between Ravita, Kavita and Babita will be :
sub_questions.solution:
Old ratio of Ravita, Savita, Kavita, Babita = 5:3:2:2. 
Savita's share = 3/12. It is acquired equally by Ravita, Kavita, and Babita.
Each acquires = 3/12 * 1/3 = 1/12.
New share of Ravita = 5/12 + 1/12 = 6/12.
New share of Kavita = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12.
New share of Babita = 2/12 + 1/12 = 3/12.
New Ratio = 6:3:3, which simplifies to 2:1:1. The correct option is A.

questions.text: फर्म के विघटन के समय ₹ 15,000 की एक अलिखित परिसम्पत्ति थी, जिसे एक साझेदार द्वारा ₹ 13,000 में ले लिया गया। साझेदार के पूँजी खाते के नाम पक्ष में खतौनी की जाएगी :
questions.text_english: On dissolution of a firm, there was an unrecorded asset of ₹15,000 which was taken over by a partner at ₹ 13,000. Partner's capital account will be debited by:
questions.solution: When a partner takes over an asset (whether recorded or unrecorded) upon the dissolution of a firm, their Capital Account is debited with the agreed value at which the asset is taken over. Here, the agreed value is ₹ 13,000. Therefore, the Partner's Capital Account will be debited by ₹ 13,000. The correct option is D.
questions.solution_hindi: जब किसी फर्म के विघटन पर कोई साझेदार किसी संपत्ति (चाहे वह दर्ज हो या अलिखित) को ले लेता है, तो उस संपत्ति के सहमत मूल्य से उसके पूँजी खाते को डेबिट किया जाता है। यहाँ सहमत मूल्य ₹ 13,000 है। इसलिए, साझेदार का पूँजी खाता ₹ 13,000 से डेबिट किया जाएगा। सही विकल्प D है।

questions.text: सन तथा मून एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि बराबर-बराबर विभाजित करते थे। उनकी प्रत्येक की स्थायी पूँजी ₹ 5,00,000 थी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए खाते तैयार करने के पश्चात, यह ज्ञात हुआ कि साझेदारी संलेख के अनुसार पूँजी पर 10% वार्षिक दर से ब्याज की खतौनी साझेदारों के चालू खातों के जमा पक्ष में नहीं की गई। इसको शुद्ध करने की समायोजन प्रविष्टि होगी :
questions.text_english: Sun and Moon were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Their fixed capitals were ₹ 5,00,000 each. After the accounts for the year ended $31^{st}$ March, 2024 were prepared, it was discovered that interest on capital @ 10% p.a. was not credited to the partners' current accounts as provided in the partnership deed. The rectifying adjustment entry for the same will be :

options_english.B: Sun's Current A/c Dr. 50,000; To Moon's Current A/c 50,000
options_english.C: Moon's Current A/c Dr. 50,000; To Sun's Current A/c 50,000
options_english.D: Sun's Current A/c Dr. 50,000; Moon's Current A/c Dr. 50,000; To Profit and Loss Appropriation A/c 1,00,000

questions.solution:
Interest on capital to be provided = 10% of ₹ 5,00,000 = ₹ 50,000 for each partner. Total interest = ₹ 1,00,000. 
If interest on capital was not provided, the profits distributed were higher by ₹ 1,00,000. These excess profits were distributed in their profit-sharing ratio, which is equal (1:1). 
So, excess profit credited to each = ₹ 50,000.
Now, if we correct this, we need to debit each partner for the excess profit (₹ 50,000) and credit them for the interest on capital (₹ 50,000). 
Net effect for Sun = 50,000 (Cr) - 50,000 (Dr) = Nil. 
Net effect for Moon = 50,000 (Cr) - 50,000 (Dr) = Nil. 
Since the net effect on each partner's account is zero, no rectifying entry is required. The correct option is A.
questions.solution_hindi: प्रत्येक साझेदार के लिए पूँजी पर ब्याज = ₹ 5,00,000 का 10% = ₹ 50,000। कुल ब्याज = ₹ 1,00,000। यदि पूँजी पर ब्याज नहीं दिया गया, तो बाँटा गया लाभ ₹ 1,00,000 अधिक था। यह अतिरिक्त लाभ उनके लाभ-विभाजन अनुपात (1:1) में बाँटा गया था। इसलिए, प्रत्येक के खाते में जमा अतिरिक्त लाभ = ₹ 50,000। सुधार के लिए, प्रत्येक को अतिरिक्त लाभ (₹ 50,000) के लिए डेबिट करना होगा और ब्याज (₹ 50,000) के लिए क्रेडिट करना होगा। सन के लिए शुद्ध प्रभाव = 50,000 (क्रेडिट) - 50,000 (डेबिट) = शून्य। मून के लिए शुद्ध प्रभाव = शून्य। चूँकि शुद्ध प्रभाव शून्य है, इसलिए किसी प्रविष्टि की आवश्यकता नहीं है। सही विकल्प A है।

questions.text: जॉन तथा हैरी एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि विभाजित करते थे । 1 अप्रैल, 2023 को उन्होंने दिनेश को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{1}{4}$ भाग के लिए एक नया साझेदार इस गारंटी के साथ बनाया कि लाभ में उसका न्यूनतम भाग ₹ 1,00,000 होगा। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का शुद्ध लाभ ₹ 2,80,000 था। लाभ में दिनेश को गारंटी की राशि देने के बाद फर्म के लाभ में जॉन का भाग होगा :
questions.text_english: John and Harry were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 2: 1. On $1^{st}$ April, 2023, they admitted Dinesh as a new partner for $\frac{1}{4}^{th}$ share in the profits of the firm with a guarantee that his share in the profits shall be at least ₹ 1,00,000. The net profit of the firm for the year ended $31^{st}$ March, 2024 was ₹ 2,80,000. John's share in the profits of the firm after giving the guaranteed amount of profit to Dinesh will be :
questions.solution: Total profit is ₹ 2,80,000. Dinesh's guaranteed share is ₹ 1,00,000. His calculated share would be 1/4 of ₹ 2,80,000 = ₹ 70,000, which is less than the guarantee. So, Dinesh gets the full ₹ 1,00,000. The remaining profit for John and Harry is ₹ 2,80,000 - ₹ 1,00,000 = ₹ 1,80,000. This remaining profit is distributed between John and Harry in their mutual ratio of 2:1. John's share = 2/3 of ₹ 1,80,000 = ₹ 1,20,000. The correct option is B.

sub_questions.text_english: Jeeta Ltd. forfeited 300 shares of ₹ 100 each for the non-payment of final call of ₹ 10 per share. The amount credited to share forfeiture account will be :
sub_questions.solution: The amount credited to the Share Forfeiture Account represents the amount actually received on the forfeited shares towards the face value. The face value is ₹ 100, and the unpaid final call is ₹ 10. Therefore, the amount already paid per share is ₹ 100 - ₹ 10 = ₹ 90. For 300 shares, the total amount credited to the Share Forfeiture Account is 300 shares * ₹ 90 = ₹ 27,000. Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: मीता लिमिटेड ने ₹ 10 प्रत्येक के 30,000 समता अंशों के निर्गमन के लिए आवेदन आमंत्रित किए। 29,500 अंशों के लिए आवेदन प्राप्त हुए। पूर्ण रूप से आबंटन कर दिया गया। 100 अंशों का एक अंशधारक ₹ 2 प्रति अंश की प्रथम याचना का भुगतान करने में असफल रहा। उसके अंशों का हरण कर लिया गया। ₹ 3 प्रति अंश की दूसरी याचना राशि अभी तक माँगी नहीं गई। अंशों का हरण करते समय अंश पूँजी खाते के नाम पक्ष में खतौनी की गई राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: Meeta Ltd. invited applications for issuing 30,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. Applications for 29,500 shares were received. Allotment was made in full. A shareholder holding 100 shares failed to pay the first call of ₹ 2 per share. His shares were forfeited. The second call of ₹ 3 per share was not yet made. The amount debited to share capital account, on the forfeiture of shares will be:
sub_questions.solution: When shares are forfeited, the Share Capital Account is debited with the called-up amount per share. The face value is ₹ 10, and the second call of ₹ 3 has not been made. Thus, the called-up amount is ₹ 10 - ₹ 3 = ₹ 7 per share. For the 100 forfeited shares, the total amount debited to the Share Capital Account is 100 shares * ₹ 7 = ₹ 700. Option C is correct.

sub_questions.text_english: Sudha, a partner withdrew ₹ 12,000 on $31^{st}$ October, 2023 for her personal use. Interest on drawings is charged @ 6% p.a. The interest on Sudha's drawings for the year ended $31^{st}$ March, 2024 will be :
sub_questions.solution: Interest on drawings is calculated for the period the money was utilized. Sudha withdrew the money on 31st October, 2023, and the year ends on 31st March, 2024. questions.text_english: Manoj, Dilip and Rajinder were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 7:3:5. Their fixed capitals were ₹ 10,00,000, ₹ 8,00,000 and ₹ 6,00,000, respectively. The partnership deed provided for interest on partners' drawings @ 12% p.a. Which of the following accounts will be debited for charging interest on partners' drawings?
questions.solution: When interest is charged on partners' drawings, it is a gain for the firm. The entry is to debit the Partners' Current Account (or Capital Account if fluctuating) and credit the Interest on Drawings Account. Wait, the question asks which account is debited to *charge* interest. The partner's current account is debited. None of the options list Current Account. Let's re-read. When interest on drawings is transferred to P&L Appropriation, Interest on Drawings A/c is debited and P&L App A/c is credited. However, if the question means the initial charge, the partner's account is debited. If capitals are fixed, it should be Current A/c. Since Current A/c is missing, the most appropriate answer in context of closing entries could be 'Interest on Drawings Account' which is debited when transferred to P&L Appropriation. Let's re-read carefully: "Which of the following accounts will be debited for charging interest on partners' drawings?". Usually, Partner's Current A/c is debited. Since the options are limited and capital is fixed, charging it to Capital A/c is wrong. The entry is Partner's Current A/c Dr. To Interest on Drawings. Then Interest on Drawings A/c Dr. To P&L Appropriation. So Interest on Drawings Account is debited to transfer the balance to P&L Appropriation. Therefore, option B or C might be intended. The CBSE marking scheme for similar questions has pointed to the partner's current account, but if absent, the process of charging to P&L App debits Interest on Drawings. Let's assume the question meant closing entry, so C.

questions.text: रमन, हरी तथा सुरेश की साझेदारी फर्म के विघटन पर वसूली व्यय ₹ 17,000 का भुगतान फर्म की तरफ से ₹ 75,000 के एक देनदार ने किया। देरी से भुगतान के कारण ₹ 2,000 के ब्याज के साथ उससे शेष राशि प्राप्त हुई। वसूली खाता _______ से _______ किया जाएगा।
questions.text_english: On the dissolution of the partnership firm of Raman, Hari and Suresh, realisation expenses ₹ 17,000 were paid by a debtor of ₹ 75,000 on behalf of the firm. The remaining amount was received from him along with interest of ₹ 2,000 for delayed payment. Realisation Account will be _______ by _______
questions.solution: The debtor owed ₹ 75,000. He paid ₹ 17,000 as realisation expenses on behalf of the firm. This effectively reduces his debt to ₹ 58,000. He paid this remaining amount along with ₹ 2,000 interest, making the cash received by the firm ₹ 60,000. The entire cash received from asset realization (including interest) is credited to the Realisation Account. Thus, the Realisation Account is credited by ₹ 60,000. The correct option is D.
questions.solution_hindi: देनदार पर ₹ 75,000 बकाया था। उसने फर्म की ओर से ₹ 17,000 के वसूली व्यय का भुगतान किया। इससे उसका ऋण घटकर ₹ 58,000 रह गया। उसने ₹ 2,000 ब्याज के साथ शेष राशि का भुगतान किया, जिससे फर्म को प्राप्त नकद राशि ₹ 60,000 हो गई। संपत्ति की वसूली से प्राप्त नकद राशि को वसूली खाते में जमा (credit) किया जाता है। अतः वसूली खाता ₹ 60,000 से क्रेडिट किया जाएगा। सही विकल्प D है।

questions.text: पैराटिग्म लिमिटेड ने ₹ 100 प्रत्येक के 40,000, 11% ऋणपत्रों का निर्गमन 5% छूट पर किया, जिनका शोधन प्रीमियम पर किया जाएगा। इन ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर 'ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर हानि खाता' के नाम पक्ष में ₹ 4,00,000 से खतौनी की गई। ऋणपत्रों के शोधन पर प्रीमियम की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Paratigm Ltd. issued 40,000, 11% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 5%, redeemable at a premium. On issue of these debentures 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account' was debited with ₹ 4,00,000. The amount of premium on redemption of debentures was:
questions.solution:
The 'Loss on Issue of Debentures Account' aggregates both the discount on issue and the premium payable on redemption. 
Total face value of debentures = 40,000 * ₹ 100 = ₹ 40,00,000. 
Discount on issue (5%) = 5% of ₹ 40,00,000 = ₹ 2,00,000. 
Total Loss on Issue given = ₹ 4,00,000. 
Premium on redemption = Total Loss - Discount on Issue = ₹ 4,00,000 - ₹ 2,00,000 = ₹ 2,00,000. 
Thus, the correct option is B.
questions.solution_hindi:
ऋणपत्रों के निर्गमन पर हानि खाते में निर्गमन पर बट्टा और शोधन पर प्रीमियम दोनों शामिल होते हैं। 
ऋणपत्रों का कुल अंकित मूल्य = 40,000 * ₹ 100 = ₹ 40,00,000. 
निर्गमन पर छूट (5%) = ₹ 40,00,000 का 5% = ₹ 2,00,000. 
कुल हानि = ₹ 4,00,000. 
शोधन पर प्रीमियम = कुल हानि - निर्गमन पर छूट = ₹ 4,00,000 - ₹ 2,00,000 = ₹ 2,00,000. 
अतः सही विकल्प B है।

X Ltd. invited applications for issuing 90,000 equity shares of ₹ 100 each. The amount per share was payable as follows:
On Application ₹ 20
On Allotment ₹ 50
On First and final call Balance
Applications for 2,00,000 shares were received. An applicant who had applied for 5,000 shares paid the entire share money with the application. The total application money received by the company was:
questions.solution:
The company received base application money for 2,00,000 shares. Base application money = 2,00,000 * ₹ 20 = ₹ 40,00,000. 
In addition, one applicant who applied for 5,000 shares paid the entire share money in advance. The total value of a share is ₹ 100. The advance amount per share is the sum of allotment and calls = ₹ 100 - ₹ 20 = ₹ 80. 
Advance money received = 5,000 * ₹ 80 = ₹ 4,00,000.
Total money received at the time of application = Base application money + Advance money = ₹ 40,00,000 + ₹ 4,00,000 = ₹ 44,00,000. 
The correct option is A.

questions.text_english: A, B and C were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:5:3. It was decided that with effect from $1^{st}$ April, 2024, profits and losses will be shared in the ratio of 6:5:5. Due to change in the profit sharing ratio, A's gain or sacrifice will be :
questions.solution:
A's old share = 8 / (8+5+3) = 8/16. A's new share = 6 / (6+5+5) = 6/16. 
A's Sacrifice = Old Share - New Share = 8/16 - 6/16 = 2/16, which simplifies to 1/8. 
Since the result is positive, it is a sacrifice. Therefore, A sacrifices 1/8. Option C is correct.

(ii) 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म ने ₹ 60,000 का लाभ अर्जित किया।
questions.text_english:
Suman and Lata were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 2. On $1^{st}$ April, 2023, their capital accounts showed balances of ₹ 1,50,000 and ₹ 2,00,000, respectively. The partnership deed provided for interest on capital @ 8% p.a. Show the treatment of interest on capital in the following cases if:
(i) The firm earned a profit of ₹ 14,000 for the year ended $31^{st}$ March, 2024.
(ii) The firm earned a profit of ₹ 60,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2024.

key_points: Calculate full interest on capital: Suman = ₹ 1,50,000 * 8% = ₹ 12,000. Lata = ₹ 2,00,000 * 8% = ₹ 16,000. Total required = ₹ 28,000.

Case (i): Available profit (₹ 14,000) is less than required interest (₹ 28,000). Profit is distributed in the ratio of claims (12:16 or 3:4). Suman receives ₹ 14,000 * 3/7 = ₹ 6,000. Lata receives ₹ 14,000 * 4/7 = ₹ 8,000.

Case (ii): Available profit (₹ 60,000) is sufficient. Full interest is provided. Suman receives ₹ 12,000. Lata receives ₹ 16,000. The remaining profit (₹ 32,000) is distributed in profit-sharing ratio (3:2).

questions.solution:
First, calculate the full interest on capital for each partner as per the deed.
Suman's interest = 8% of ₹ 1,50,000 = ₹ 12,000.
Lata's interest = 8% of ₹ 2,00,000 = ₹ 16,000.
Total interest on capital required = ₹ 12,000 + ₹ 16,000 = ₹ 28,000.

Case (i): The profit earned is ₹ 14,000. Since the available profit is less than the total interest on capital required, the available profit will be distributed in the ratio of their respective interest claims (i.e., capital ratio).
Ratio of claims = 12,000 : 16,000 = 3:4.
Interest allowed to Suman = ₹ 14,000 * (3/7) = ₹ 6,000.
Interest allowed to Lata = ₹ 14,000 * (4/7) = ₹ 8,000.

Case (ii): The profit earned is ₹ 60,000. Since this is sufficient to cover the total interest, full interest will be provided.
Interest allowed to Suman = ₹ 12,000.
Interest allowed to Lata = ₹ 16,000.
The remaining profit (₹ 60,000 - ₹ 28,000 = ₹ 32,000) will be transferred to the partners' capital accounts in their profit-sharing ratio (3:2).

sub_questions.text_english:
Abha and Sara were partners in a firm. Their capitals were: Abha ₹ 3,00,000 and Sara ₹ 2,00,000. The normal rate of return in similar business is 10%. The profits of the firm of Abha and Sara for the last three years were:
2021-22 ₹ 60,000
2022-23 ₹ 90,000
and 2023-24 ₹ 1,20,000
Calculate goodwill of the firm on the following basis:
(i) Four years purchase of the average profits for the last three years.
(ii) Capitalisation of super-profits.

key_points: (i) Goodwill by Average Profit Method: Average Profit * Number of years' purchase = 90,000 * 4 = ₹ 3,60,000.
Calculate Capital Employed: 3,00,000 + 2,00,000 = ₹ 5,00,000.
Calculate Normal Profit: 5,00,000 * 10% = ₹ 50,000.
Calculate Super Profit: Average Profit - Normal Profit = 90,000 - 50,000 = ₹ 40,000.
(ii) Goodwill by Capitalisation of Super Profit Method: Super Profit * (100 / Normal Rate of Return) = 40,000 * (100 / 10) = ₹ 4,00,000.

sub_questions.solution:
First, we calculate the Average Profit for the last three years.
Total Profit = ₹ 60,000 + ₹ 90,000 + ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 2,70,000.
Average Profit = ₹ 2,70,000 / 3 = ₹ 90,000.

(i) Goodwill at four years' purchase of average profits:
Goodwill = Average Profit × Number of years' purchase
Goodwill = ₹ 90,000 × 4 = ₹ 3,60,000.

(ii) Goodwill by Capitalisation of super-profits:
Capital Employed = Abha's Capital + Sara's Capital = ₹ 3,00,000 + ₹ 2,00,000 = ₹ 5,00,000.
Normal Profit = Capital Employed × (Normal Rate of Return / 100)
Normal Profit = ₹ 5,00,000 × (10 / 100) = ₹ 50,000.
Super Profit = Average Profit - Normal Profit
Super Profit = ₹ 90,000 - ₹ 50,000 = ₹ 40,000.
Goodwill = Super Profit × (100 / Normal Rate of Return)
Goodwill = ₹ 40,000 × (100 / 10) = ₹ 4,00,000.

On Kamal's admission, the goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 6,00,000. Kamal brought his share of goodwill premium in cash.
(i) Calculate the sacrificing ratio.
(ii) Pass necessary journal entries for the treatment of goodwill on Kamal's admission.

key_points: Calculate Sacrifice/Gain = Old Share - New Share. Vijay = 5/10 - 4/10 = 1/10 (Sacrifice). Ravi = 3/10 - 2/10 = 1/10 (Sacrifice). Raman = 2/10 - 3/10 = -1/10 (Gain).
Sacrificing ratio of Vijay and Ravi is 1:1.
Calculate Kamal's share of goodwill = 6,00,000 * 1/10 = ₹ 60,000.
Calculate Raman's required contribution for his gain = 6,00,000 * 1/10 = ₹ 60,000.

Old Ratio of Vijay, Ravi, and Raman = 5:3:2 (out of 10).

Sacrifice = Old Share - New Share

Total amount to be credited to sacrificing partners = ₹ 60,000 (from Kamal) + ₹ 60,000 (from Raman) = ₹ 1,20,000.

sub_questions.text_english: KM Ltd. acquired assets worth ₹ 7,20,000 and took over liabilities of ₹ 2,00,000 of LS Ltd. for a purchase consideration of ₹ 9,60,000. KM Ltd. issued 12% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 4% in favour of LS Ltd. for payment of purchase consideration. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of KM Ltd.

key_points: Determine Net Assets acquired: Assets (7,20,000) - Liabilities (2,00,000) = 5,20,000.
Compare with Purchase Consideration (9,60,000). The excess 4,40,000 is treated as Goodwill.
Record acquisition: Debit Assets (7.2L), Debit Goodwill (4.4L), Credit Liabilities (2L), Credit LS Ltd (9.6L).
Calculate number of debentures: 9,60,000 / 96 (Issue price) = 10,000 debentures.
Record payment: Debit LS Ltd (9.6L), Debit Discount on Issue of Debentures (40k), Credit 12% Debentures A/c (10L).

sub_questions.solution:
When acquiring a business, if the purchase consideration exceeds the net value of assets taken over, the difference is recorded as Goodwill. Net Assets = Assets (₹ 7,20,000) - Liabilities (₹ 2,00,000) = ₹ 5,20,000. The purchase consideration is ₹ 9,60,000. Thus, Goodwill = ₹ 9,60,000 - ₹ 5,20,000 = ₹ 4,40,000.

The purchase consideration is settled by issuing debentures at a 4% discount. The issue price per debenture is ₹ 100 - ₹ 4 = ₹ 96. The number of debentures issued = Total consideration / Issue price = ₹ 9,60,000 / ₹ 96 = 10,000 debentures. The total discount is 10,000 × ₹ 4 = ₹ 40,000.

     To LS Ltd.                                   ₹ 9,60,000
(Being assets and liabilities taken over and balance transferred to goodwill)

2. LS Ltd.                       Dr. ₹ 9,60,000
   Discount on Issue of Deb. A/c Dr. ₹ 40,000
     To 12% Debentures A/c                        ₹ 10,00,000
(Being 10,000, 12% debentures of ₹ 100 each issued at a discount of 4% to discharge the purchase consideration)

questions.text: अमन, गोविन्द तथा गुरु एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3: 2 : 1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। सुदर्शन को फर्म के लाभों में $\frac{1}{4}$ भाग के लिए प्रवेश दिया गया। अमन, गोविन्द, गुरु तथा सुदर्शन के बीच 9: 5:4 : 6 के नए लाभ विभाजन अनुपात पर सहमति हुई। यह सहमति हुई कि नई फर्म की कुल पूँजी ₹ 3,60,000 होगी। सुदर्शन इसका $\frac{1}{4}$ भाग अपनी पूँजी के रूप में लाएगा। अन्य साझेदारों की पूँजी का समायोजन भी नए लाभ विभाजन अनुपात में किया जाना था। सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात अमन, गोविन्द तथा गुरु की पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 60,000, ₹ 80,000 तथा ₹ 45,000 थीं। अमन, गोविन्द तथा गुरु की नई पूँजी की गणना कीजिए। उपर्युक्त लेनदेनों के लिए फर्म की पुस्तकों में आवश्यक रोज़नामचा प्रविष्टियाँ भी कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Aman, Govind and Guru were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Sudarshan was admitted for $\frac{1}{4}th$ share in the profits of the firm. The new profit sharing ratio between Aman, Govind, Guru and Sudarshan was agreed at 9: 5:4:6. The total capital of the new firm was agreed upon as ₹ 3,60,000. Sudarshan will bring $\frac{1}{4}$ th of this as his capital. The capitals of the other partners were also to be adjusted according to the new profit sharing ratio. The capitals of Aman, Govind and Guru after all adjustments stood at ₹ 60,000, ₹ 80,000 and ₹ 45,000 respectively. Calculate the new capitals of Aman, Govind and Guru. Also pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of the firm.

key_points: Determine cash to be brought in or withdrawn by comparing adjusted capitals with new capitals. Aman: 1,35,000 - 60,000 = 75,000 (Bring in). Govind: 75,000 - 80,000 = 5,000 (Withdraw). Guru: 60,000 - 45,000 = 15,000 (Bring in).
Journal Entry 1: Sudarshan brings capital. Bank A/c Dr 90,000 To Sudarshan's Capital A/c 90,000.
Journal Entry 2: Adjustments for Aman and Guru bringing cash. Bank A/c Dr 90,000 To Aman's Capital A/c 75,000, To Guru's Capital A/c 15,000.
Journal Entry 3: Adjustment for Govind withdrawing cash. Govind's Capital A/c Dr 5,000 To Bank A/c 5,000.

questions.solution:
Working Notes:
The total capital of the new firm is fixed at ₹ 3,60,000.
The new profit-sharing ratio is Aman : Govind : Guru : Sudarshan = 9 : 5 : 4 : 6. The total parts are 9 + 5 + 4 + 6 = 24.
The new capitals are calculated by dividing the total capital according to the new ratio:
Aman's New Capital = ₹ 3,60,000 × 9/24 = ₹ 1,35,000
Govind's New Capital = ₹ 3,60,000 × 5/24 = ₹ 75,000
Guru's New Capital = ₹ 3,60,000 × 4/24 = ₹ 60,000
Sudarshan's Capital = ₹ 3,60,000 × 6/24 = ₹ 90,000

Now, we compare the existing adjusted capitals with the required new capitals to find the deficit or surplus:
Aman: Required = ₹ 1,35,000, Existing = ₹ 60,000. Deficit = ₹ 75,000 (Needs to bring in cash).
Govind: Required = ₹ 75,000, Existing = ₹ 80,000. Surplus = ₹ 5,000 (Will withdraw cash).
Guru: Required = ₹ 60,000, Existing = ₹ 45,000. Deficit = ₹ 15,000 (Needs to bring in cash).

Journal Entries:
1. Bank A/c                          Dr.  ₹ 90,000
     To Sudarshan's Capital A/c                  ₹ 90,000
(Being capital brought in by Sudarshan)

2. Bank A/c                          Dr.  ₹ 90,000
     To Aman's Capital A/c                       ₹ 75,000
     To Guru's Capital A/c                       ₹ 15,000
(Being cash brought in by Aman and Guru to make their capitals proportionate)

3. Govind's Capital A/c              Dr.  ₹ 5,000
     To Bank A/c                                 ₹ 5,000
(Being excess capital withdrawn by Govind)

questions.text_english:
Madhavan, Chatterjee and Pillai were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in ratio of 2: 1: 2. On 31st March, 2024, their Balance Sheet was as follows:
Balance Sheet of Madhavan, Chatterjee and Pillai as at $31^{st}$ March, 2024

On the above date, the firm was dissolved and the following transactions took place:
(i) Debtors were taken over by the creditors in full settlement of their account.
(ii) Madhavan agreed to pay Mrs. Madhavan's loan.
(iii) 50% of the stock was taken over by Chatterjee at 10% less than the book value. The remaining stock was sold at a profit of 20%.
(iv) Land and Building was taken over by Pillai for ₹ 10,00,000 and Plant and Machinery was sold as scrap for ₹ 20,000.
(v) Realisation expenses ₹ 17,000 were paid by cheque.
Prepare Realisation Account.

key_points: Transfer assets to Realisation A/c debit side: Debtors 95,000; Stock 2,20,000; Land and Building 1,82,000; Plant and Machinery 1,00,000. Total = 5,97,000.
Transfer external liabilities to Realisation A/c credit side: Creditors 1,10,000; Outstanding Expenses 17,000; Mrs. Madhavan's Loan 2,00,000; Provision for Doubtful Debts 5,000. Total = 3,32,000.
(i) Creditors took over debtors in full settlement: No journal entry is required for the settlement. No further payment to creditors is needed.
(ii) Mrs. Madhavan's loan taken by Madhavan: Debit Realisation A/c by 2,00,000 (To Madhavan's Capital A/c).

(iii) Stock realization: Total 2,20,000. 50% = 1,10,000 taken by Chatterjee at 10% discount = 99,000. Credit Realisation A/c by 99,000 (By Chatterjee's Capital A/c). Remaining 1,10,000 sold at 20% profit = 1,32,000. Credit Realisation A/c by 1,32,000 (By Bank A/c).
(iv) Land & Building taken by Pillai for 10L: Credit Realisation A/c by 10,00,000 (By Pillai's Capital A/c). Machinery sold for 20k: Credit Realisation A/c by 20,000 (By Bank A/c).
(v) Realisation expenses paid: Debit Realisation A/c by 17,000 (To Bank A/c).

Settle remaining liabilities: Outstanding Expenses (17,000) and Chatterjee's Loan. Note: Partner's loan is not transferred to Realisation. Outstanding expenses are paid in full. Debit Realisation A/c by 17,000 (To Bank A/c).

Calculate final profit/loss: Total Debit = 5,97,000 (assets) + 2,00,000 (Mrs M loan) + 17,000 (exp) + 17,000 (O/s exp) = 8,31,000. Total Credit = 3,32,000 (liab) + 99,000 (Chatterjee) + 1,32,000 (Bank) + 10,00,000 (Pillai) + 20,000 (Bank) = 15,83,000. Net Profit = 15,83,000 - 8,31,000 = 7,52,000.
Distribute Profit to partners in 2:1:2: Madhavan = 3,00,800; Chatterjee = 1,50,400; Pillai = 3,00,800. Debit Realisation A/c by 7,52,000.

questions.solution:
The Realisation Account is prepared by first transferring all asset accounts (excluding cash at bank) and external liability accounts (excluding partner's loan and capitals) to it.
Debit side transfers: Debtors ₹ 95,000; Stock ₹ 2,20,000; Land and Building ₹ 1,82,000; Plant and Machinery ₹ 1,00,000. Total Assets transferred = ₹ 5,97,000.
Credit side transfers: Creditors ₹ 1,10,000; Outstanding Expenses ₹ 17,000; Mrs. Madhavan's Loan ₹ 2,00,000; Provision for Doubtful Debts ₹ 5,000. Total Liabilities transferred = ₹ 3,32,000.

Now processing the transactions:
(i) Debtors taken over by creditors in full settlement: No entry is passed in the Realisation Account for this exchange. No further payment to creditors is needed.
(ii) Mrs. Madhavan's loan paid by Madhavan: Debit Realisation A/c with 'To Madhavan's Capital A/c' for ₹ 2,00,000.
(iii) Stock (Book Value ₹ 2,20,000): 
   - 50% taken by Chatterjee = ₹ 1,10,000. Taken at 10% less = ₹ 99,000. Credit Realisation A/c 'By Chatterjee's Capital A/c' for ₹ 99,000.
   - Remaining 50% sold at 20% profit = ₹ 1,10,000 + 20% = ₹ 1,32,000. Credit Realisation A/c 'By Bank A/c' for ₹ 1,32,000.
(iv) Land and Building taken by Pillai for ₹ 10,00,000: Credit Realisation A/c 'By Pillai's Capital A/c' for ₹ 10,00,000. 
   - Machinery sold for ₹ 20,000: Credit Realisation A/c 'By Bank A/c' for ₹ 20,000.
(v) Realisation expenses paid: Debit Realisation A/c 'To Bank A/c' for ₹ 17,000.

We must also pay off any unaddressed external liabilities. Outstanding Expenses were not addressed, so they are paid in full. Debit Realisation A/c 'To Bank A/c' for ₹ 17,000.

Balancing the Realisation Account:
Total Credit = 3,32,000 + 99,000 + 1,32,000 + 10,00,000 + 20,000 = ₹ 15,83,000.
Total Debit = 5,97,000 + 2,00,000 + 17,000 + 17,000 = ₹ 8,31,000.
Net Profit on Realisation = ₹ 15,83,000 - ₹ 8,31,000 = ₹ 7,52,000.
This profit is distributed to the partners in the ratio 2:1:2.
Madhavan's share = ₹ 7,52,000 × 2/5 = ₹ 3,00,800.
Chatterjee's share = ₹ 7,52,000 × 1/5 = ₹ 1,50,400.
Pillai's share = ₹ 7,52,000 × 2/5 = ₹ 3,00,800.
The debit side records 'To Profit transferred to Partners' Capital A/cs' for these amounts, balancing both sides at ₹ 15,83,000.

questions.text_english: ABC Ltd. was registered with authorised capital of ₹ 1,00,00,000 divided into 10,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. On $1^{st}$ April, 2024, the company offered to the public for subscription, 1,00,000 shares. Applications for 99,000 shares were received and allotment was made in full to all the applicants. sub_questions.text: कम्पनी की अधिकृत पूँजी है :
sub_questions.text_english: The authorised capital of the company is:
sub_questions.solution: The passage explicitly states that the company was registered with an authorised capital of ₹ 1,00,00,000 divided into 10,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each. Thus, option C is correct.

sub_questions.text: एबीसी लिमिटेड की निर्गमित पूँजी है :
sub_questions.text_english: The issued capital of ABC Ltd. is :
sub_questions.solution: The issued capital represents the portion of the authorised capital that the company formally offers to the public for subscription. The company offered 1,00,000 shares of ₹ 10 each. Therefore, the issued capital is 1,00,000 shares × ₹ 10 = ₹ 10,00,000. Option D is correct.

sub_questions.text: अदत्त याचना की राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of calls-in-arrears will be :
sub_questions.solution: Calls-in-arrears represents the amount called up by the company but not yet paid by the shareholders. Here, a shareholder holding 9,000 shares failed to pay the final call of ₹ 3 per share. Thus, the calls-in-arrears amount to 9,000 × ₹ 3 = ₹ 27,000. Option A is correct.

sub_questions.text: एबीसी लिमिटेड की 'अभिदत्त एवं पूर्ण प्रदत्त पूँजी' होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The 'subscribed and fully paid up capital' of ABC Ltd. will be :
sub_questions.solution: The 'subscribed and fully paid up capital' represents the shares for which the entire called-up amount has been received. The total subscribed shares are 99,000. The shares on which the full amount is not paid are 9,000. Therefore, the number of fully paid shares is 99,000 - 9,000 = 90,000 shares. The fully paid capital is 90,000 shares × ₹ 10 = ₹ 9,00,000. Option B is correct.

sub_questions.text: एबीसी लिमिटेड की 'अभिदत्त लेकिन पूर्ण प्रदत्त नहीं पूँजी' होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: 'Subscribed but not fully paid up capital' of ABC Ltd. will be :
sub_questions.solution: The 'subscribed but not fully paid up capital' is calculated for those shares where the full called-up amount hasn't been received. There are 9,000 such shares. The gross amount for these shares is 9,000 × ₹ 10 = ₹ 90,000. The unpaid calls-in-arrears (calculated previously) are ₹ 27,000. The net amount shown under this heading is ₹ 90,000 - ₹ 27,000 = ₹ 63,000. Option D is correct.

sub_questions.text: एबीसी लिमिटेड के स्थिति विवरण में दर्शाई जाने वाली 'अंश पूँजी' की राशि होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The amount of 'Share Capital' presented is the Balance Sheet of ABC Ltd. will be:
sub_questions.solution: The total amount of 'Share Capital' disclosed on the face of the Balance Sheet is the sum of 'subscribed and fully paid up capital' and 'subscribed but not fully paid up capital'. This is ₹ 9,00,000 + ₹ 63,000 = ₹ 9,63,000. Alternatively, it can be calculated as total called-up capital minus calls-in-arrears: (99,000 * 10) - 27,000 = ₹ 9,90,000 - ₹ 27,000 = ₹ 9,63,000. Option A is correct.

questions.text_english:
Statement I: In case of non-financial enterprises, payment of interest and dividends are classified as financing activities, whereas receipt of interest and dividends are classified as investing activities.
Statement II: Investing and financing transactions that require the use of cash or cash equivalents, should be excluded from cash flow statement.

questions.solution: Statement I is true; for a non-financial enterprise, paying interest and dividends is related to the funds borrowed (financing), while receiving them is related to funds invested elsewhere (investing). Statement II is false because the primary purpose of the Cash Flow Statement is exactly to include and report transactions that DO require the use of cash or cash equivalents. key_points: Calculate Net Profit Before Tax: Change in Surplus (17,00,000 - 8,00,000) = 9,00,000. Add back Interim Dividend paid (1,20,000). Net Profit Before Tax = ₹ 10,20,000.

sub_questions.solution:
To calculate Cash Flows from Operating Activities, we start by determining the Net Profit Before Tax and Extraordinary Items.
The closing balance of the Statement of P&L is ₹ 17,00,000, and the opening balance is ₹ 8,00,000. The difference is ₹ 9,00,000. 
We add back the interim dividend paid during the year, which is an appropriation of profit, amounting to ₹ 1,20,000.
Net Profit Before Tax = ₹ 9,00,000 + ₹ 1,20,000 = ₹ 10,20,000.

Next, we make adjustments for non-cash and non-operating items.
Patents decreased from ₹ 50,000 to Nil. Assuming they were amortised/written off, this non-cash expense is added back.
Operating Profit before Working Capital changes = ₹ 10,20,000 + ₹ 50,000 = ₹ 10,70,000.

Now we adjust for changes in working capital (Current Assets and Current Liabilities, excluding cash equivalents).
- Sundry Debtors increased from ₹ 4,20,000 to ₹ 5,80,000. An increase in current assets is a cash outflow. Less: Increase in Debtors = (₹ 1,60,000).
- Sundry Creditors increased from ₹ 60,000 to ₹ 1,40,000. An increase in current liabilities is a cash inflow. Add: Increase in Creditors = ₹ 80,000.

Calculate Cash Flows from Investing Activities.

key_points: Sale of Machinery: Book value = Cost (1,40,000) - Acc Dep (90,000) = 50,000. Sold at a gain of 10,000. Sale proceeds = 50,000 + 10,000 = ₹ 60,000 (Inflow).

Calculate purchase of machinery by preparing Machinery Account (at cost): Opening Bal = 50,00,000. Credit side: Bank A/c (sale) 60,000, Acc Dep A/c 90,000, P&L A/c (gain) goes to debit side. Or simpler: Credit side transfer to disposal = Cost = 1,40,000. Closing Bal = 70,00,000. Debit side = Op Bal 50,00,000. Balancing figure (Purchase) = 70L + 1.4L - 50L = ₹ 21,40,000 (Outflow).
Net Cash from Investing Activities = Inflow from Sale (60,000) - Outflow for Purchase (21,40,000) = (₹ 20,80,000) Outflow.

sub_questions.solution:
To calculate cash flows from investing activities, we must determine the cash inflows from sales and cash outflows for purchases related to non-current assets.

First, we analyze the sale of machinery.
The original cost of the machine sold is ₹ 1,40,000.
The accumulated depreciation on this specific machine is ₹ 90,000.
The Book Value at the time of sale = ₹ 1,40,000 - ₹ 90,000 = ₹ 50,000.
It was sold at a gain of ₹ 10,000. Therefore, the Sale Proceeds (Cash Inflow) = Book Value + Gain = ₹ 50,000 + ₹ 10,000 = ₹ 60,000.

Next, we determine the purchase of new machinery by preparing the Machinery Account at Cost.
Opening Balance (31.3.2023) = ₹ 50,00,000.
The cost of the machine sold is credited to this account to remove it from the books = ₹ 1,40,000.
The Closing Balance (31.3.2024) is ₹ 70,00,000.
To balance the account (Opening Bal - Cost of Sold Machine + Purchases = Closing Bal):
₹ 50,00,000 - ₹ 1,40,000 + Purchases = ₹ 70,00,000.
Purchases = ₹ 70,00,000 + ₹ 1,40,000 - ₹ 50,00,000 = ₹ 21,40,000. This represents a Cash Outflow.

Net Cash Flow from Investing Activities:
Proceeds from sale of Machinery: ₹ 60,000 (+)
Payment for purchase of Machinery: ₹ 21,40,000 (-)
Net Cash Used in Investing Activities = ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 21,40,000 = (₹ 20,80,000).

questions.text_english: Explain the ways in which accounting software provide data security, safety and confidentiality.

key_points: Password Control: Restricts access to authorized personnel only, requiring unique user IDs and passwords.
Data Encryption: Scrambles the stored financial data so that it cannot be read or understood if accessed directly from the backend without authorization.
Data Audit/Audit Trail: Maintains a detailed log of every action taken within the software, tracking who entered or modified data and at what time, ensuring accountability.
Data Vault/Backups: Provides secure mechanisms to regularly back up data, preventing loss due to hardware failure or corruption.

questions.solution:
Accounting software ensures the security, safety, and confidentiality of critical financial data through several robust mechanisms:

1. Password Protection and Access Control: The system acts as a gatekeeper, requiring authorized users to log in with a unique username and secure password. Furthermore, administrators can assign specific 'roles' to users, ensuring an employee only sees the data necessary for their job, thereby maintaining strict confidentiality.
2. Data Encryption: To protect against external hacking or data theft, the software encrypts the database. This means the raw financial numbers and texts are converted into an unreadable cipher. Even if a malicious actor accesses the backend storage, they cannot read the actual data without the decryption key.
3. Data Audit Trails: The software automatically generates a secure, unalterable log of all user activities. It records exactly who logged in, what transactions they entered or modified, and the exact timestamp. This trail is crucial for internal checks, preventing fraud, and ensuring total accountability and data safety.

questions.solution:
In standard computerized accounting software, particularly systems widely used in India like Tally, there is a built-in hierarchy to classify ledger accounts efficiently. 

There are exactly 28 pre-defined account groups provided by default in the software. These pre-defined groups eliminate the need for users to create a basic accounting structure from scratch. 

These 28 groups are further sub-divided based on their structural role into two categories:
1. Primary Groups: There are 15 Primary Groups. These are the top-level categories that directly define the nature of an account. Of these 15, 9 are balance sheet groups (e.g., Capital, Current Assets) and 6 are income statement groups (e.g., Direct Incomes, Indirect Expenses).
2. Sub-groups: There are 13 Sub-groups. These act as secondary, more specific categories that reside underneath the Primary Groups (e.g., 'Sundry Debtors' is a sub-group situated under the primary group 'Current Assets').

sub_questions.text_english: State the steps to prepare a chart.

key_points: Step 1: Enter or organize the data into an Excel worksheet in a tabular format.
Step 2: Highlight/select the specific range of data cells that need to be plotted, including column and row headers if required for labels.
Step 3: Navigate to the 'Insert' tab on the Excel ribbon at the top of the window.
Step 4: Locate the 'Charts' group on the ribbon.
Step 5: Click on the icon representing the desired chart type (e.g., Column, Line, Pie, Bar).
Step 6: Select the specific sub-type (e.g., 2D Clustered Column) from the drop-down menu to insert the chart onto the worksheet.

sub_questions.solution:
Creating a chart in spreadsheet software like MS Excel involves a few straightforward steps to translate raw data into a visual format. The standard steps are:

1. Prepare the Data: First, ensure the numerical data is logically organized into columns and rows within the worksheet. Include clear headings, as these will serve as labels in the chart.
2. Select the Data Range: Click and drag to highlight the specific block of cells containing the data you wish to visualize, ensuring you encompass the relevant row and column titles.
3. Access the Insert Tab: Move your cursor to the main ribbon at the top of the screen and click on the 'Insert' tab.
4. Choose Chart Type: Within the 'Insert' tab, locate the dedicated 'Charts' group. Here, you will see icons for various chart types like Column, Line, Pie, and Scatter.
5. Insert the Chart: Click on the icon of the chart type that best suits your data. A drop-down menu will appear offering various styles (e.g., 2D or 3D). Click your preferred style, and the chart will instantly be generated and embedded into your worksheet.

sub_questions.text_english: What is meant by internal margin while using MS Excel ? State the options available.

key_points: Internal Margin refers to the blank space or padding between the text inside a shape/textbox and the outer border of that shape/textbox.
It controls how closely the text sits next to the edge of the object containing it.
The options available to adjust internal margins are: Left, Right, Top, and Bottom margins.

sub_questions.solution:
When working with shapes, text boxes, or chart elements in MS Excel, the term 'Internal Margin' refers to the invisible padding or empty buffer space situated between the text contained within the element and the actual outer border or boundary of that element. It functions similarly to cell padding in a table, ensuring the text doesn't touch the lines, which improves readability and aesthetic appeal.

Excel provides granular control over this spacing. A user can independently adjust the following four options for internal margins within the 'Format Shape' or 'Format Text Box' dialogue:
1. Left Margin: Controls the space between the text and the left edge.
2. Right Margin: Controls the space between the text and the right edge.
3. Top Margin: Controls the space between the upper text line and the top edge.
4. Bottom Margin: Controls the space between the lowest text line and the bottom edge.

questions.text_english: = SUM (B2B3) will give an error while using a spreadsheet. Identify the error and state the steps to correct it.

key_points: Error Identification: The formula will return a #NULL! error (or potentially a #NAME? error if the software interprets it as an unknown named range, but generally it's a syntax error due to missing operator). The primary issue is a missing reference operator (like a colon or comma) between the cell references B2 and B3.
Step 1: Click on the cell displaying the error to select it.
Step 2: Click inside the Formula Bar located at the top of the worksheet to edit the formula.
Step 3: Insert the correct mathematical or reference operator between B2 and B3. If the intent is to sum a continuous range from B2 to B3, insert a colon ':' so the formula reads =SUM(B2:B3).
Step 4: If the intent is to sum only two individual disparate cells B2 and B3, insert a comma ',' so the formula reads =SUM(B2,B3).
Step 5: Press 'Enter' to execute the corrected formula.

questions.solution:
Error Identification:
When a user types `=SUM(B2B3)` in a spreadsheet, the software cannot parse the argument because it lacks a required mathematical or reference operator between the two cell addresses. Excel will typically interpret "B2B3" as an undefined name and return a `#NAME?` error, or if interpreted as an invalid intersection, a `#NULL!` error. The fundamental mistake is a syntax error caused by a missing separator.

Steps to Correct the Error:
1. Select the Cell: Click on the specific cell that is displaying the error message to make it active.
2. Access the Formula Bar: Move your cursor to the Formula Bar at the top of the screen where `=SUM(B2B3)` is visible, and click inside the parentheses between 'B2' and 'B3'.
3. Insert the Correct Operator: You must define how the function should handle the cells by inserting an operator:
   - To sum a range: If you want to add all cells from B2 down to B3, insert a colon (`:`). The corrected formula becomes `=SUM(B2:B3)`.
   - To sum individual cells: If you want to add only the specific values in cell B2 and cell B3, insert a comma (`,`). The corrected formula becomes `=SUM(B2,B3)`.
4. Execute: Press the 'Enter' key on your keyboard. The software will recalculate the formula and display the correct numerical sum.
